applies_to: ACI B6 gas transmitters carrying two gas sensors (B6M main sensor plus a Q6R second sensor) on BACnet MS/TP.
summary: The B6 is a two-sensor gas transmitter (electrochemical toxic, catalytic combustible or NDIR CO2/CH4 sensors) that talks BACnet MS/TP as an end device. Each sensor reports its reading, STEL, TWA, 24-hour peak and board temperature as analog inputs, with eight alarm-status BVs per sensor (BV 0-7 and 8-15); three relay and three buzzer outputs are binary outputs (BO 0-5).
notes: The PICS prints the binary objects only as ranges: BV 0-7 "B6M Alarm1 to Alarm8 Status", BV 8-15 "Q6R Alarm1 to Alarm8 Status", BO 0-2 "Relay1 to Relay3 Status" and BO 3-5 "Buzzer1 to Buzzer3 Status". Only the first object of each range is listed here; the rest follow the same pattern (BV 0+x = main-sensor Alarm(x+1), BV 8+x = second-sensor Alarm(x+1), BO x = Relay(x+1), BO 3+x = Buzzer(x+1)).
The per-object pages for the Q6R inputs repeat instances 0-4 by mistake; the PICS object list places them at AI 5-9, which is used here.
Object names in the PICS have a leading space on some B6M inputs; it is dropped here.
Gas readings are listed in parts-per-million for every sensor type; check the actual units on combustible (%LEL) sensors.
The binary objects carry a priority array (B6 writes at priority 12) but Present_Value is listed as read-only.
MS/TP master or slave, 9600-76800 baud; no segmentation.

source.title: B6 Dual-Sensor Gas Transmitter BACnet Protocol Implementation Conformance (PIC) Statement

integration.summary: Set the MS/TP address on the transmitter, discover device 4005 (default) and read the two concentration inputs plus the alarm-status BVs. There are no BMS commands; the relays and buzzers are driven by the transmitter's own alarm levels.
setup: Device object default instance 4005; device name and description include the MS/TP MAC address and gas types.
MS/TP master or slave at 9600, 19200, 38400 or 76800 baud; max master 127, max info frames 1.
gotchas: Which alarm level each AlarmN BV represents is set in the transmitter; the PICS does not define them.
Units read parts-per-million for all inputs in the PICS; verify for combustible sensors.
